explanations: Green lies between cyan and yellow on the visible spectrum, and chlorophyll is by far its largest source in nature.
White is the lightest colour and has no chroma at all, because a white object reflects and scatters every visible wavelength.
Orange sits between yellow and red on the spectrum and is named after the fruit.
The national flag of Ireland is a vertical tricolour of green at the hoist, then white, then orange, and is half as high as it is wide.

sources.excerpt: Green is the color between cyan and yellow on the visible spectrum.
By far the largest contributor to green in nature is chlorophyll, the chemical by which plants photosynthesize and convert sunlight into chemical energy.
White is the lightest color and is achromatic (having no chroma).
White objects fully (or almost fully) reflect and scatter all the visible wavelengths of light.
Orange is the colour between yellow and red on the spectrum of visible light.
It is named after the fruit of the same name.
The orange colour of many fruits and vegetables, such as carrots, pumpkins, sweet potatoes, and oranges, comes from carotenes, a type of photosynthetic pigment.

The national flag of Ireland (Irish: bratach na hÉireann), frequently referred to in Ireland as "the tricolour" (an trídhathach) and elsewhere as the Irish tricolour, is a vertical tricolour of green (at the hoist), white and orange.
